thread:
Maria: heads-up — canary rolled 2025-11-05 is showing a p99 jump on short-seq textgen workloads. baseline 82ms -> 215ms :eyes:
Akshay: uhoh. any obvious change in the rollout notes? which services effected?
Maria: only runtime-hosted pool A (gcp-eu-west1), qps same. traces show bigger time inside kernel selection + KV cache stalls. attaching quick numbers.
perf-bot: CI perf job #1623 failed for commit b2c4d9a (merge). p99 210ms (+160%). see https://ci.internal/reports/1623
Taylor: can you paste the profile snippet?
Maria: sure — here's the flame sample from our microbench (short prompt, seq=128, batch=4):
```
hot path: kernel_selector.cpp:470 (+43%)
  -> choose_kernel_for_seq (45% samples)
  -> batching_heuristics.cpp:213 (20%)
  -> kv_cache_manager.cpp:138 (12%)
mallocs: small spike in ~512b allocations during kv populate
```
Sasha: interesting — kernel_selector change was in the batching heuristics PR 9f3a7..b2c4d (the merge). Could be the heuristics now prefer the fallback kernel for mid-length sequences.
Akshay: I remember a tweak to prefer single-stream kernels when batch < 3. If heuristics mis-evaluate sequence distribution we could be degrading for batch=4.
Leo: KV hit-rate drop? what are the numbers?
Maria: pre-merge kv hit ~92% on prefix reuse, post-merge ~38% for same traces. So a lot more cache invalidations / cold loads.
Taylor: that smells like a change in the cache key composition or a subtle canonicalization bug. Did anyone touch kv key hashing recently?
Sasha: not in the batching PR. There was a tiny tweak in the request-context fingerprinting in commit 4c1b9 that landed two commits earlier — it reorders metadata fields used in cache key construction. Could be related.
Akshay: plan: we need a quick git-range to bisect. suspect range is from commit 4c1b9..b2c4d (includes fingerprint tweak + batching merge). I can start a git bisect run using the perf runner on a bench node.
Maria: sweet. reproduction steps I used locally:
```
# on perf-node-12
git checkout <commit>
python infra/bench/perf_runner.py --model redwood-open-7b --seq 128 --batch 4 --iters 200 --profile out.svg
# then check p99 in out.svg or infra/bench/last_result.json
```
Akshay: I'll run `git bisect start` with good=9a7e2 (pre-change) bad=b2c4d9a (current) and use `git bisect run ./infra/bench/local-bench.sh`. local-bench.sh exits 0 if p99 <= 100ms, 1 otherwise.
Leo: note: local-bench machines need CUDA kernels built with our dev flags. I'll make a snapshot with the correct env and add to the bisect job.
Taylor: while Akshay runs that, I'll instrument extra logging in kernel_selector to log chosen kernel id + sequence len distribution, and add a quick metric to KV cache probe to emit hit/miss ratio per-request-id. We can add them temporarily to the canary.
Sasha: if bisect points at 4c1b9 (fingerprint reorder) then it's KV key bug, quick revert will restore perf. If it points at the batching merge commit then heuristics revert/patch required.
Akshay: starting bisect now. kicking off on perf-node-12. Will post updates, ETA ~45-60m since each run compiles a wheel. :hammer:
perf-bot: bisect job started (job id 9873). logs: https://ci.internal/bisect/9873
Maria: in parallel, I'm going to pin canary to tag `release-2025-11-01` and hold the rollout for additional regions. We don't want this hitting prod.
Leo: creating a k8s rollout block until we have root cause. I'll set an automated revert trigger if p99 > 150ms for 10m in any zone.
Akshay: update — bisect narrowed to commit range 4c1b9..a8e5f. Current good still 9a7e2. continuing.
Taylor: dropped a debug shard to canary with kernel_selector verbose logs. small overhead but will tell us if fallback kernel chosen more frequently.
Maria: quick datapoint from canary logs — fallback kernel chosen 67% of the time post-merge vs 11% pre-merge.
Sasha: OK that matches the kernel selection theory. But why did fallback cause KV miss wave? maybe fallback interacts with batched prefix handling and triggers extra context evictions.
Akshay: bisect completed — culprit commit: 4c1b9a7 (the fingerprint reorder). Reproducer exit status 1 on that commit, 0 on parent.
Taylor: confirmed locally; swapping back to old key composition restores KV hitrate and p99 to ~84ms.
Maria: great find. action items:
- Akshay: open a revert PR for 4c1b9a7 and tag rollback candidate. (assigned)
- Taylor: prepare a proper fix that keeps the intended metadata order but makes key canonicalization stable (avoid order-sensitive serialization).
- Leo: keep canary pinned and rollout blocked until revert lands and passes perf smoke.
- Sasha: add unit tests for key canonicalization + a perf regression test to catch this class.
Akshay: created PR #5983 revert 4c1b9a7 — running CI. CC @Taylor for follow-up fix PR.
perf-bot: PR #5983 CI step perf-smoke passed on build 1896. merged.
Maria: canary metrics after revert: p99 86ms, kv hit-rate 90%. rolling unhold once we watch for 30 minutes. :thumbsup:
Taylor: I'll land a non-rollback patch today to canonicalize keys (stable sort of meta fields + protobuf bytes normalization).
Sasha: adding regression test to infra which runs perf_runner for seq=128 and asserts kv hit >= 80% for sample trace.
Leo: thanks everyone. postmortem draft please — we need to call out lacking perf gate for key-shape sensitive changes.
Maria: will start a short incident write-up and link the bisect logs + PRs. good job team.
Akshay: thanks — glad bisect pointed cleanly.
Maria: closing thread once the postmortem is linked and rollout fully unblocked.
